source.statement: alpha>=0, alpha-convex f, supplied gradient flow and attained minimum z; gap(t)<=alpha/(2(exp(alpha*t)-1))*norm(X0-z)^2. At alpha0 source explicitly interprets coefficient as1/(2t).
source.proof: Squared distance to z has derivative<=-alpha distance²-2gap(s) by first-order convexity. Gronwall with time-dependent gap forcing; objective descent bounds earlier gap below by terminal gap; evaluate exponential integral.
source.regularity: Source C2 Euclidean f, classical supplied forward curve, standing attained minimum.

endpoint_source_gap.finding: Source says all t>=0 but the real quotient is singular at t0, including stated alpha0 limit1/(2t).
endpoint_source_gap.required_scope: Use strictly positive observation time t>0 for the normalized value bound and retain this as an explicit source endpoint qualification. Do not silently use Lean total division at0.
endpoint_source_gap.counterexample_to_literal_Lean_t0: f(x)=x²/2, X(t)=exp(-t), z0, alpha1. At t0 the initial gap is1/2, but the raw Lean quotient1/(2(exp0-1))=0, so the purported all-nonnegative-time formula becomes1/2<=0.
endpoint_source_gap.alpha0: Use the direct branch coefficient1/(2t), proved by K0 comparison. No analytic alpha→0 limit theorem is needed for the case split; do not claim such a limit has been formalized.
endpoint_source_gap.alternative: A division-free weighted inequality can include t0 vacuously, but normalized source rate still requires t>0.
endpoint_source_gap.publication: Record the t0 source gap and its exact positive-time target boundary; any claimed repair overlay requires separate independent source review.

candidate_assessment.conclusion: Nonnegative gap bounded by norm(X0-z)^2/(2t) if alpha0, otherwise alpha*norm(X0-z)^2/(2(exp(alpha*t)-1)).
candidate_assessment.substantive_delta: Derive actual objective monotonicity and squared-distance forcing from the supplied gradient trajectory and first-order convexity; these combine into a source-shaped value-rate adapter. Scalar Gronwall/integral manipulation alone is existing background, not new progress.

accepted_route: Derive actual right derivative d/ds f(Xs)=-norm(gradient f(Xs))² via Frechet/curve chain rule.
Use existing scalar one-sided Gronwall on arbitrary[s,t] with K0,epsilon0 to prove f(Xt)<=f(Xs) for0<=s<=t<=T. This avoids assuming unavailable ordinary interior derivatives.
Differentiate norm(Xs-z)² using HasDerivWithinAt.sub_const and norm_sq. Apply ASTIS firstOrder_lower_bound_of_strongConvexOn at Xs,z to get D prime(s)<=-alpha D(s)-2gap(s).
For a fixed terminal t>0, monotonicity gives gap(s)>=gap(t), so D prime(s)<=-alpha D(s)-2gap(t) on0t.
Apply existing scalar le_gronwallBound_of_liminf_deriv_right_le with K=-alpha and epsilon=-2gap(t). Its epsilon is an arbitrary real, so negative forcing is allowed; avoid norm variants.

Use D(t)>=0. For alpha0, gronwallBound_K0 yields2t gap(t)<=D0. For alpha>0, explicit nonzero-K bound gives2gap(t)(1-exp(-alpha*t))<=alpha D0 exp(-alpha*t); multiply by exp(alpha*t), divide by positive denominator.
Use global minimum for nonnegative gap. Restrict hX continuity from0T to0t; no derivative at terminal t or T needed.
